supported_frameworks: IEC 62443-3-3 (System Security Requirements and Security Levels)
NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 (Guide to Operational Technology Security)
NERC CIP-005-7 (Cyber Security — Electronic Security Perimeter(s))

SL-1.target_level: Security Level 1 — Protection Against Casual or Coincidental Violation
SL-1.adversary_profile: Non-malicious operator error, accidental misrouting, or broadcast storms.
SL-1.minimum_boundary_mechanism: VLAN logical segmentation (IEEE 802.1Q) and basic Layer 3 ACLs.

SL-2.target_level: Security Level 2 — Protection Against Intentional Violation Using Simple Means
SL-2.adversary_profile: Opportunistic cybercriminals or insiders with low resources, commodity malware, and generic network scanning tools.
SL-2.minimum_boundary_mechanism: Industrial Stateful Firewall / Next-Gen Firewall (NGFW) in Purdue Level 3.5 DMZ with explicit allow-listing.
SL-2.why_software_firewalls_cap_at_sl2: Software firewalls run complex multi-million-line OS kernels and stateful packet-inspection engines over bidirectional Ethernet PHYs. They remain vulnerable to zero-day firewall OS CVEs, stolen admin credentials, misconfigured bi-directional rules (e.g., opening TCP 135/445/502 inward), and encrypted command-and-control return channels.

SL-3.target_level: Security Level 3 — Protection Against Sophisticated Means & IACS-Specific Skills
SL-3.adversary_profile: Organized ransomware syndicates and targeted OT threat groups possessing ICS protocol payloads (Modbus/IEC-104/DNP3 injectors), stolen IT domain admin credentials, and NGFW bypass techniques.
SL-3.minimum_boundary_mechanism: Physical Layer-1/2 Hardware Data Diode (ARCH_A, ARCH_B, ARCH_C) for telemetry conduits, or Dual-Stage Hardware-Isolated Controlled Gateway with mandatory OT-originated session lock and deterministic command whitelisting (ARCH_D) where closed-loop dispatch is operationally mandatory.
SL-3.engineering_justification: Eliminates IP routing and TCP session pass-through across the IT/OT boundary. Even full compromise of the Corporate IT Active Directory and DMZ Replica Server yields zero inbound network path into Level 0–3 OT control assets.

SL-4.target_level: Security Level 4 — Protection Against State-Sponsored Actors with Extended Resources
SL-4.adversary_profile: Nation-state APT actors with custom zero-day firewall firmware exploits, supply-chain implants, and physical-consequence sabotage objectives (grid blackout, safety system override).
SL-4.minimum_boundary_mechanism: Pure Unidirectional Layer-1/2 Hardware Data Diode (ARCH_A, ARCH_B, ARCH_C) enforcing one-way physical transmission (OS-less FPGA / optical coupling with physically absent return transmit circuitry).
SL-4.engineering_justification: Enforces unidirectionality via laws of physics at Layer 1/2 rather than software policy. No software vulnerability, kernel exploit, or misconfiguration on the IT side can transmit a single bit backward across the physical isolation barrier.

IEC_62443_3_3.standard_name: ISA/IEC 62443-3-3: System Security Requirements and Security Levels

requirements.title: Network Segmentation
requirements.base_requirement: The control system shall logically segment control system networks from non-control system networks and logically segment critical control system networks from other control system networks.

requirement_enhancements.SR 5.1 RE 1: Physical network segmentation — Physically segment control system networks from non-control system (Corporate IT) networks (Required for SL-2+).
requirement_enhancements.SR 5.1 RE 2: Independence from non-control system networks — Ensure the control system operates independently without reliance on Corporate IT network services (DNS, AD, SMB) across the boundary (Required for SL-3/SL-4).
requirement_enhancements.SR 5.1 RE 3: Logical and physical isolation of critical networks — Physically isolate safety-critical and high-consequence OT zones from all untrusted networks (Required for SL-4).

requirements.diode_satisfaction_statement: Deploying Hardware Isolation Archetypes A/B/C/D physically terminates Layer 2/Layer 3 Ethernet switching and IP routing between OT and IT, achieving SR 5.1 RE 1, RE 2, and RE 3.

requirements.title: Zone Boundary Protection
requirements.base_requirement: The control system shall monitor and control communications at zone boundaries to enforce the compartmentalization defined in the risk-based zone and conduit model.

requirement_enhancements.SR 5.2 RE 1: Deny by default, allow by exception — Block all cross-zone traffic by default and permit only explicitly defined application payloads.
requirement_enhancements.SR 5.2 RE 2: Island mode — Provide the capability to prevent any communication through the zone boundary during cyber emergencies without disrupting local OT control.
requirement_enhancements.SR 5.2 RE 3: Fail close — Ensure boundary protection devices fail in a closed state prohibiting unauthorized packet forwarding upon power loss or fault (Required for SL-3/SL-4).

requirements.diode_satisfaction_statement: OS-less Layer-1/2 hardware barriers block 100% of inbound packets unconditionally, terminate TCP sessions on dedicated TX/RX proxies, and inherently fail closed on power loss without degrading local OT PLC polling.

requirements.title: Malicious Code Protection
requirements.base_requirement: The control system shall provide protection mechanisms to prevent, detect, and mitigate the effects of malicious code at all entry and exit points (conduits).

requirement_enhancements.SR 3.2 RE 1: Malicious code protection on entry and exit points — Enforce deterministic payload sanitization and block executable/ransomware propagation across conduits.

requirements.diode_satisfaction_statement: Severing SMBv1/RDP/DCOM and enforcing unidirectional protocol-breaking TX->RX serialization physically prevents IT ransomware (WannaCry, LockBit, Industroyer2) from traversing into OT zones.

requirements.title: Continuous Monitoring
requirements.base_requirement: The control system shall provide the capability to continuously monitor all security mechanism performance and export audit/telemetry events safely.

requirement_enhancements.SR 6.2 RE 1: Zero-exposure telemetry export — Export Syslog, IDS/SPAN alerts, and Historian metrics to enterprise SOC/SIEM without opening inbound SOC-to-OT firewall rules.

requirements.diode_satisfaction_statement: UDP Syslog and SPAN telemetry traverse one-way across Diode TX -> RX to enterprise SIEM collectors with zero return path.

NIST_SP_800_82_REV3.standard_name: NIST Special Publication 800-82 Rev. 3: Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security

requirements.title: OT Network Architecture, DMZ & Unidirectional Gateways
requirements.summary: Recommends strict separation of OT and corporate IT networks using an Industrial DMZ (Purdue Level 3.5) and explicitly highlights optical/hardware Unidirectional Gateways (Data Diodes) paired with DMZ Replica Servers for high-impact OT environments.
key_mandates: Prohibit direct connections from Corporate IT (Level 4) into OT Control Zones (Levels 0–3); all shared data must terminate in a DMZ replica.
Eliminate dual-homed hosts (servers with two NICs bridging IT and OT subnets) as they completely bypass perimeter boundary enforcement.
Use hardware-enforced Unidirectional Gateways where TX agents poll OT controllers locally and replicate state one-way to DMZ Historians, preventing inbound polling and exploit propagation.
related_nist_800_53_r5_controls: SC-7(4) Boundary Protection — External Telecommunications Services
AC-4(4) Information Flow Enforcement — Hardware Unidirectional Flow Control

NERC_CIP_005_7.standard_name: NERC CIP-005-7: Cyber Security — Electronic Security Perimeter(s) (North American Bulk Electric System)

requirements.title: Electronic Security Perimeter (ESP) & Access Point Justification

parts.Part 1.1: All applicable BES Cyber Systems shall reside within a defined Electronic Security Perimeter (ESP).
parts.Part 1.2: All External Routable Connectivity must pass through an identified Electronic Access Point (EAP).
parts.Part 1.3: Require explicit inbound and outbound access permissions and documented operational justification for every permitted port/protocol; deny all other traffic by default.

requirements.diode_impact: Replacing bidirectional EAP firewall rules with a Layer-1/2 Hardware Data Diode (ARCH_A / ARCH_C) eliminates inbound External Routable Connectivity entirely, substantially reducing NERC CIP audit scope and inbound attack surface.

requirements.title: Interactive Remote Access (IRA) Management

parts.Part 2.1: Utilize an Intermediate System such that the Cyber Asset initiating Interactive Remote Access does not directly access an applicable BES Cyber Asset.
parts.Part 2.2: Enforce encryption and multi-factor authentication for all permitted Interactive Remote Access; prohibit unauthorized direct RDP/SSH/Telnet/VNC into the ESP.

requirements.diode_impact: Physically severs unauthorized inbound RDP (3389), SSH (22), Telnet (23), and VNC (5900) sessions at Layer 1/2.

INDIA_CEA_AND_NCIIPC.standard_name: India Central Electricity Authority (CEA) Cyber Security in Power Sector Guidelines (2021) & NCIIPC Protected System Directives

requirements.title: Mandatory Unidirectional Gateway / Data Diode Isolation for OT/SCADA
requirements.summary: Mandates that Responsible Entities operating Generation, Transmission (220kV/400kV/765kV substations), Distribution, and Load Despatch Centres (SLDC/RLDC/NLDC) isolate OT/SCADA/SAS networks from Corporate IT networks.
key_mandates: Any data transfer between the OT/SCADA Electronic Security Perimeter and external Corporate IT or enterprise reporting networks MUST pass through a hardware-enforced Unidirectional Security Gateway (Data Diode) where one-way visibility suffices.
Strict prohibition on dual-homed workstations, split-tunnel VPNs, and unauthorized internet/IT bridges connected to Substation Automation Systems (IEC-104 / IEC-61850 / DNP3).
One-way security log forwarding from OT switches/relays to centralized SOC/CSIRT for CERT-In compliance without opening inbound SOC-to-OT ports.

requirements.control_id: NCIIPC CII Guidelines & IT Act Sec 70A/70B
requirements.title: Protection of National Critical Information Infrastructure (Power, Energy, Water, Manufacturing, Transport)
requirements.summary: Requires deterministic defense-in-depth architecture, physical zone segregation of critical control loops, elimination of legacy unauthenticated protocols across boundaries, and verifiable pre-cutover testing.

finding_to_control_mappings.description: Corporate IT or DMZ host initiates TCP SYN connections inward into OT VLANs to poll PLCs, RTUs, or OPC servers (e.g., Modbus FC 03/04, IEC-104 interrogation, SQL SELECT).
finding_to_control_mappings.remediation_statement: Reverse polling direction via Hardware Data Diode TX Inner Proxy (polls OT devices locally on OT LAN) and RX Replica Server (serves read-only replica to IT Historian with zero inbound OT packets).

finding_to_control_mappings.description: Legacy Microsoft OPC Classic (DCOM TCP 135 + dynamic ephemeral ports 49152–65535) traversing the IT/OT boundary, forcing wide-open firewall pinholes.
finding_to_control_mappings.remediation_statement: Deploy an OT-local OPC-DA-to-OPC-UA wrapper adjacent to the legacy OPC server, converting dynamic DCOM traffic to static TCP 4840 OPC-UA fed into Hardware Diode TX Proxy.

finding_to_control_mappings.description: Cross-zone Windows SMB/CIFS file sharing (TCP 445/139) enabling direct ransomware worm propagation between Corporate IT and OT servers.
finding_to_control_mappings.remediation_statement: Physically sever TCP 445/139 via Hardware Data Diode and migrate batch CSV/recipe log transfers to unidirectional SFTP push relay across Diode TX -> RX.

finding_to_control_mappings.description: Server or engineering workstation equipped with dual network interfaces bridging both an OT control VLAN and Corporate IT VLAN, completely bypassing the perimeter firewall.
finding_to_control_mappings.remediation_statement: Disconnect the IT-facing NIC immediately and route all Historian/SCADA data extraction exclusively through the Hardware Data Diode conduit.

finding_to_control_mappings.description: Inbound interactive administrative sessions (RDP 3389, SSH 22, Telnet 23, VNC 5900, TeamViewer) originating from Corporate IT into OT assets.
finding_to_control_mappings.remediation_statement: Physically sever all inbound interactive remote access at Layer 1/2 via Hardware Data Diode; restrict engineering changes to supervised local OT consoles.

finding_to_control_mappings.description: Inbound actuation or register-write function codes (Modbus FC 05/06/15/16, IEC-104 C_SC_NA_1) sent from untrusted IT hosts to Level 1 PLCs/RTUs.
finding_to_control_mappings.remediation_statement: Enforce Layer-1/2 physical unidirectionality (ARCH_A or ARCH_C) to make inbound register overwrites physically impossible; if verified closed-loop MES/AGC dispatch is required, isolate on ARCH_D with OT-originated session lock and strict register whitelisting.

finding_to_control_mappings.description: Active PLC, camera, or gateway discovered in switch ARP/MAC tables or packet captures that is absent from the facility's official network architecture diagram.
finding_to_control_mappings.remediation_statement: Incorporate shadow asset into the reconciled Purdue L0–L5 asset inventory, assign to an explicit IEC 62443 Security Zone, and route external telemetry through the sized Hardware Data Diode.

finding_to_control_mappings.description: High-bandwidth IP CCTV cameras (RTSP/ONVIF) or BACnet HVAC controllers with vulnerable embedded firmware routed through corporate switches to IT NVR/VMS servers.
finding_to_control_mappings.remediation_statement: Isolate camera/BMS VLAN behind ARCH_B_VIDEO_IOT_DIODE (1 Gbps unidirectional media/IoT proxy), streaming RTSP/BACnet one-way to corporate VMS while blocking camera-pivot lateral movement.

finding_to_control_mappings.description: Critical OT zone relies solely on a stateful software firewall (capped at IEC 62443 SL-2) rather than physical Layer-1/2 unidirectional isolation.
finding_to_control_mappings.remediation_statement: Upgrade critical IT/OT conduits from software-only firewall filtering (SL-2) to OS-less Layer-1/2 Hardware Data Diodes (SL-4).
